title: A table has a header row with a toggle for rules between its rows
body:
coax draws a table with no header row. A code block has one, as in `┌ rust   wrap pan   ⧉`, and it holds the block's toggles. A toggle is a set of dim words with the active one in `accent`, and a click switches that block alone (`Toggle`, `Word` and `put_toggles` in `src/ui.rs`, with the state in `App::raw` and `App::wraps`). A table that fits the box goes into the prose's `Part::Flow`, so it has no key to hold a choice. cmr-420714 adds `rules: bool` to `cmr::Block::Table`, and with it set cmr draws a rule between body rows.

## Proposal

- Every table is a `Part::Block` with a header row `┌ table   rules`, which coax draws above cmr's rows. Selection and copy text leave the header row out.
- `rules` is dim while the table has no rules and `accent` while it has them. A click switches it. A table starts with no rules.
- `App::rules` holds the keys of the tables switched on. The `KeptBlock` holds both layouts, as it does for wrap and pan, so a click needs no new layout.

## Rejected

- The toggle at the end of the rule under the table's header, or a header row shown only while the mouse is over the table. Jack chose a header row on every table.
- Rules on from the start. A table of one-line rows would grow to nearly twice its height.

## Cost

- Each table takes one more row on screen.
- The wrap and pan words of coax-a03507 would go in this header row too.
